transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Brooks (Redwood AE), Daniel Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Jenna Morales (OrbitCare Procurement), Rajiv Patel (CTO), Sara Liu (Legal), Mike Tran (Security)

Optional summary:
- Purpose: Final procurement/legal review for MSA + DPA + SLAs, confirm pricing band and onboarding steps.
- Outcome: Redwood to provide redlined MSA/DPA and SOC2 artifacts; schedule technical benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Brooks: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll wait a minute for folks to pop in. This is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the deal, with me is Daniel our solutions engineer and Priya CSM.
[00:10] Jenna Morales: Hi Maya, Jenna here. We have Rajiv, Sara and Mike on our side. Thanks for making time.
[00:16] Rajiv Patel: afternoon all.
[00:18] Maya Brooks: Awesome. Quick agenda — cover MSA redlines, DPA specifics around ePHI, SLA targets and then pricing approvals and onboarding timeline. Sound good?
[00:27] Sara Liu: yes sounds good. We circulated a few redlines earlier, i'll call them out.
[00:31] Daniel Reed: great, i'll jump in on the technical bits — encryption, keys, VPC and staging.
[00:37] Mike Tran: and i'll focus on security posture questions, logging and audit.

[00:45] Maya Brooks: Perfect. Sara, can you start with the top MSA points you want to confirm?
[00:49] Sara Liu: sure, the main things for us: liability cap needs to be raised for regulated data, we want stronger data deletion language, and an indemnity carve out for HIPAA related claims. Also need clarity on subprocessor list and notification windows for changes. Some of those you already provided but we flagged a few gaps.
[01:12] Maya Brooks: understood. On liability cap we typically follow the standard SOW-based caps, but we can discuss exceptions for regulated workloads. I'll note that and get legal to propose language. For subprocessor notifications we have a 30-day notice and can supply the subprocessor list — Daniel can share the vendor list post-call.
[01:32] Daniel Reed: yes i'll export our current subproc list, it includes cloud infra partners and monitoring vendors. we'll mark which handle ePHI.
[01:40] Rajiv Patel: on the DPA itself — we need explicit mention of ePHI handling and encryption at rest + in transit with customer-managed keys. We can't have Redwood hold root key material.
[01:52] Daniel Reed: we support customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and HSM-backed options. For private deployments we can do an on-prem HSM or bring-your-own-key via our KMS connector. There was a small note in our docs about rotating keys and key access — i'll pull that into a doc for you.
[02:14] Mike Tran: can you confirm whether the KV cache in the runtime ever writes unencrypted data to disk? We need to know about any plaintext traces.
[02:22] Daniel Reed: good question. The runtime keeps KV cache in memory; if we spill to disk for high memory pressure, it uses encrypted swap and it's covered by the same disk encryption controls. For dedicated/private deployments we can guarantee no spill to disk if you require that.
[02:37] Mike Tran: ok we might ask for a config that disables disk spill for our pilot.
[02:41] Maya Brooks: noted. Sara any additional legal redlines on the DPA?
[02:46] Sara Liu: breach notification timeline — we asked for 48 hours. Your standard is 72, can you come down to 48 for ePHI incidents?
[02:54] Priya Shah: we have flexibility depending on severity and contract terms. For ePHI we understand shorter timelines are important. We'll flag procurement/legal to prioritize the redline.
[03:06] Sara Liu: also need audit support — SOC2 Type II report and willingness to allow either onsite or remote audit of controls, or at minimum supply evidence and subcontractor assurances.
[03:18] Maya Brooks: yes we can supply SOC2 Type II report and summary, and Daniel will provide the control matrix plus a runbook for remote evidence. For onsite audits we need to check the operational logistics — some customers do remote attestation.
[03:30] Daniel Reed: i'll attach the SOC2 summary and notes on what we can provide remotely. We also have pen test summaries and third-party scan summaries.
[03:38] Rajiv Patel: about SLAs — we currently need 99.9% availability for inference endpoints and latency p95 under 300ms for our top-traffic routes. Can you commit to that on Dedicated or Host with Dedicated capacity?
[03:51] Maya Brooks: for Dedicated we offer SLA tiers that can hit 99.9% and latency SLOs are achievable depending on model and batch settings. We'll add an SLA section to the SOW that ties to Dedicated capacity and a performance SLO tied to a benchmark set.
[04:05] Daniel Reed: to be explicit: latency depends on model size, quantization and sequence length. For your shorter prompts we can reach p95 under 300ms on a dedicated pool with tuned batching and prefix caching. We'll run a benchmark with your representative prompt set to validate.
[04:21] Rajiv Patel: that benchmark is critical before procurement signs off. We need a run-without-production-data option, but with production-like traffic.
[04:29] Daniel Reed: understood. We can run a synthetic benchmark and a later pilot with masked or synthetic ePHI to mirror distribution. We'll share the benchmarking plan in doc form.
[04:36] Jenna Morales: on pricing — procurement asked the finance team for a few clarifications. You provided a banded pricing sheet; we need a firm rate for the first 12 months for budgeting and an approval doc for our finance approvers. Also any volume discounts or committed utilization tiers?
[04:52] Maya Brooks: yes our pricing works with monthly committed spend for Dedicated. We can convert the band into a firm 12-month quote tied to a committed capacity. There are standard volume bands with step-down pricing at 3T tokens and 10T tokens usage equivalents. We'll produce a formal quote for your approvers.
[05:07] Jenna Morales: what's the lead time for Dedicated capacity once PO is issued?
[05:12] Priya Shah: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region. We'll confirm after the SOW is signed; there is an option for burst capacity to cover initial ramp.
[05:21] Mike Tran: network and VPC — we need information on how Redwood connects to our VPC, IP allow lists, and whether there's a transit gateway requirement. Also SAML SSO for admin console and RBAC enforcement.
[05:33] Daniel Reed: for Private/VPC deployments we support direct connect/Interconnect or VPN and can peering into your VPC. We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC for console and API tokens. I'll share a network diagram and the SAML metadata config.
[05:47] Rajiv Patel: good. On data residency — we need all inference for CA and EU customers to remain in region — can that be pinned?
[05:55] Maya Brooks: yes you can pin region at the routing policy level. For Dedicated we can enforce region-only routing and add contractual language for data residency.
[06:05] Sara Liu: there's also a clause about subcontractor liability — we want Redwood to remain liable for subprocessors.
[06:11] Maya Brooks: that's our standard practice; we'll add language to make that explicit.
[06:16] Jenna Morales: procurement also requested a list of references who have completed a similar security onboarding — healthcare customers preferably.
[06:23] Maya Brooks: we can share anonymized references and case studies; Daniel will point to a couple of customers in health care who did private deployments.
[06:30] Daniel Reed: yes i'll prepare a short list and redact specifics as needed.
[06:33] Priya Shah: Onboarding timeline — typically after signature we do a kickoff, then a 2-week tech setup and a 4-week pilot. We can compress to a 3-week pilot if you take burst capacity and provide an accelerated internal approval for staging access.
[06:48] Jenna Morales: procurement will need the exact SOW milestones and acceptance criteria to include in our PO.
[06:54] Maya Brooks: we'll include milestone-based acceptance in the SOW: 1) Kickoff and infra setup, 2) performance benchmark, 3) security attestation and docs, 4) pilot acceptance and sign-off.
[07:07] Sara Liu: one last legal item — data subject access and deletion processes. We want clear timelines and confirmation that Redwood will assist with any DSAR requests that touch cached tokens or logs.
[07:20] Daniel Reed: DSARs — we log requests and can correlate tokens and logs; for dedicated and private deployments we can provide tooling to search logs and purge entries. We'll document the DSAR playbook.
[07:30] Mike Tran: can you confirm log retention defaults and ability to shorten retention windows?
[07:36] Daniel Reed: default retention is 90 days for aggregated logs and 30 days for request-level traces, but we can offer custom retention up to contractual limits and offer export hooks for longer retention in your systems.
[07:49] Rajiv Patel: ok. i'd like to flag that our security council will want to run the benchmark and review the SOC2/pen test before final approval.
[07:58] Maya Brooks: that's fair. we'll prioritize providing SOC2, pen test summaries and the benchmark plan.
[08:03] Jenna Morales: timeline check — if you send docs by EOD Friday (2026-08-06), we aim to have legal/finance review completed by 2026-08-12 and then a PO the following week. Is that workable?
[08:15] Maya Brooks: yes we'll target that. I'll get the redlines and quote over by Friday.
[08:21] Priya Shah: i'll also schedule the technical benchmark with Daniel and include a pre-kickoff checklist for your infra team.
[08:28] Maya Brooks: Great. Any other blockers?
[08:30] Sara Liu: none from legal beyond the items we've discussed.
[08:33] Mike Tran: none.
[08:35] Rajiv Patel: none from engineering, thanks.
[08:37] Maya Brooks: OK thanks everyone. Quick recap and next steps — we'll send: redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 docs, vendor/subprocessor list, network diagram, pricing quote and benchmark plan. Daniel will own the tech benchmark scheduling. Sara/Jenna will send any remaining redlines by Tuesday.
[08:57] Jenna Morales: thanks all, talk soon.
[08:59] Maya Brooks: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
